_modes.execution: The skill is loaded before the run. What is scored is what the agent DOES with it: discovery, seeding, bounds, and whether the answer separates what the edges support from what they only suggest.
_modes.trigger: The run starts with NO skill preloaded and the agent is given only the user's question. What is scored is the SELECTION: whether this skill is reached for at all. An execution case cannot measure this, because loading the skill is the thing under test. Run these in a directory the skill is installed for but has not been invoked in.
_modes.regression: A fixture that asserts its own invariants and needs no agent. Run it after editing the skill's performance or bounds advice; a check that flips is the signal that the advice needs re-measuring.

_trigger_baseline.measured: 2026-09-09, against this fixture on AGE 1.6.0/PG16 and a skardi-server built from main
_trigger_baseline.trigger-row-question-must-not-select: PASS — selected no skill and refused, naming the absence of order data
_trigger_baseline.trigger-local-code-no-graph-registered: PASS — selected graph-rag, spent one `skardi schema` (exit 2), named the URL, fell back to local tools
_trigger_baseline.trigger-non-code-graph-KNOWN-FAILING: FAIL — not selected; see the case for the measurement. Needs a fixture this PR does not ship.
_trigger_baseline.note: Re-measure after any edit to the frontmatter description: that field is the whole mechanism these cases test, and it is also the field most likely to be trimmed for length.

evals.name: impact-question-needs-two-hops
evals.prompt: We're about to change how `verify_token` works. What would break? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: Discovers the graph vocabulary first (graph_schema + edge counts), then seeds on the UNIQUE key. The fixture holds two functions named `verify_token`, so an answer seeded on `name` reaches 8 dependents and one of them belongs to the other function; seeded on `fqn` it reaches 7. Expands INCOMING call edges with a bounded Cypher and reports the traversal and its bound. Must say how many of the edges it traversed are trustworthy: of the six one-hop callers, three carry `resolution: ambiguous` and three do not, so "6 dependents" presented as fact is wrong and "3 confirmed, 3 name-only matches" is right. Must not present an unordered LIMIT slice as the complete answer.

evals.name: vague-question-needs-semantic-seeding
evals.prompt: Which parts of our codebase deal with authentication, and what calls into them? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the question is too vague for a property lookup and looks for a search surface. The fixture registers a graph source and NO search surface, which is the point: the agent must discover that from `skardi schema` rather than assume it, then say what it cannot do — semantic seeding — and fall back to what the graph alone supports (enumerate candidate entities by property, e.g. files and function names under `auth`, and expand from those), labelling the coverage difference. Must not fabricate a search pipeline, and must not silently answer as if it had seeded semantically.

evals.name: row-question-should-hand-off
evals.prompt: How many orders did we get last month, broken down by status? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a rows-not-edges question and does NOT run a graph traversal. The fixture's only source is a code graph with no orders anywhere, so the correct answer names that and hands off to the retrieval skill rather than inventing a graph angle or an empty result.

evals.name: trigger-named-entity-connectivity
evals.prompt: Who calls verify_token, and what breaks if I change it? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: MUST reach for graph-rag. The question names its entity and asks for callers, which is the shape this skill exists for, and the fixture registers a graph source that `skardi schema` reports as healthy. Selecting nothing and answering from a local grep is a failure even if the local answer happens to be right: the graph holds callers a grep of the working directory cannot see. Reaching for `retrieval` is also a failure — the answer is edges, not rows.

evals.name: trigger-vague-entity-needs-seeding
evals.prompt: What handles authentication around here, and what depends on it? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: MUST reach for graph-rag. The entity is not named, so the question is the two-hop shape: find the entities first, then walk from them. Naming no skill and answering from file names is a failure. So is reaching for `auto-context`: nothing here needs an index built, and the skill that consumes an existing surface is this one.

evals.name: trigger-row-question-must-not-select
evals.prompt: How many orders did we get last month, broken down by status? Start the fixture with `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup.sh` first; it prints the server URL.
evals.expected_output: MUST NOT reach for graph-rag. The answer is rows over a table, and the presence of a graph source does not make it a connection question. `retrieval` is the right skill, and naming no skill while correctly refusing is acceptable. Loading graph-rag and then explaining that it does not apply is a weaker pass: the description is what should have prevented it.

evals.name: trigger-local-code-no-graph-registered
evals.prompt: Who calls verify_token in this repo, and what would break if I change it? Do NOT start any fixture. There is no skardi-server running.
evals.expected_output: Either outcome passes, and what is scored is the cost. Not selecting the skill and answering from the local code is correct. Selecting it is ALSO correct — the description says to reach for it even when a grep could answer, because a configured graph may hold code the working directory does not — provided the agent then spends exactly one check (`skardi schema`, exit code 2), reports the URL it tried, and falls back to the local tools. Measured cost of that path: one command, roughly five seconds. FAILURES: retrying the unreachable server, starting a server, or reporting that the question cannot be answered.

evals.name: trigger-non-code-graph-KNOWN-FAILING
evals.prompt: (Needs a fixture this PR does not ship: a graph whose vertices are documents, services or people rather than code, registered on a running server. The question is then asked in that domain's own words and mentions no graph, e.g. "this document is out of date — which other documents still point at it?")
evals.expected_output: MUST reach for graph-rag, and currently does not. Measured 2026-09-09 against a real document-reference graph (307 vertices, 393 edges) registered and healthy on a running server: asked in the domain's own words, the skill was not selected and a sibling skill matching the surface words won instead; the agent answered by full-text search plus per-document fetch, at roughly three times the wall clock and twice the cost, and silently answered from a different copy of the corpus. Prefixing the same question with "there is a graph of our documents on the server" selected it immediately. So the miss is not that the question is ambiguous — it is that the description is written almost entirely in code and Cypher vocabulary, and a non-code graph does not match it. Building this fixture is the prerequisite for fixing that, and until it exists the skill's coverage of non-code graphs is untested rather than working.

evals.name: large-graph-bounds-still-bite
evals.prompt: Run `SKARDI_SERVER_BIN=<path> SKARDI_CLI_BIN=<path> fixtures/setup_large.sh`. It builds a synthetic 50k-vertex, 250k-edge graph and asserts the bounds the small fixture cannot reach. Report which checks failed and what that means for the rules in SKILL.md.
evals.expected_output: All seven checks pass, and a failure is a finding about the skill rather than about the fixture. Each check pairs a rule with its recommended form, so a green-to-red flip means the rule stopped being load-bearing: the labeled single MATCH answers while the unlabeled split form times out; an undirected untyped `-[r]-` times out even labeled and with a LIMIT; a SQL WHERE over an unbounded view fails on max_rows while a SQL LIMIT over the same view succeeds; the truncation notice is on stderr only; and LIMIT without ORDER BY returns a visibly different slice than ORDER BY. If check 2 or 3 starts passing, the performance advice in SKILL.md needs re-timing rather than a fixture fix. Takes about ninety seconds to build and needs Docker, which is why it is not part of the default run.
